*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Pillow's contour extraction filter. Uses the fixed kernel of PIL.ImageFilter.CONTOUR to create an effect that leaves only outlines as black lines on a white background (a pen-drawing/line-art style effect).

a, b are unused (fixed kernel).

The kernel is the 3x3 [-1,-1,-1; -1,8,-1; -1,-1,-1] (scale 1, offset 255), and the output is 255 + (8*centre - sum of the 8 neighbours) saturated to 0–255. Flat areas become 255 (white), pixels darker than their surroundings become dark, and pixels brighter than their surroundings saturate at 255. In other words, a 1-pixel-wide black line sits on the "dark side" of a step while the bright side stays white (xpil_find_edges uses the same kernel with offset 0, so both sides come out bright).

The input is clipped to [0,1] and truncated after *255 into an 8-bit L image, and the output is brought back to [0,1] with /255 (introducing 1/255 quantization). The outermost 1-pixel border of the image is not filtered by Pillow and is returned with the input values. A 0-size image is rejected with a ValueError and falls back fail-soft to the clipped input (recorded in the ledger). It also responds to noise, so placing xpil_smooth_more or median before it tidies up the lines. To use the lines as regions, brighten the black-line side with invert and then feed it to threshold.

Blank frame (measured): feeding an image of uniform brightness makes every pixel foreground (1), regardless of the brightness. A frame that is blown out, occluded, or simply has no subject comes back as “100 % defective”, so test for uniformity upstream and reject such frames.
